sources.title: On the decoherence of primordial fluctuations during inflation

evidence.text: Expand interaction-picture von Neumann evolution to second order, trace environmental degrees of freedom, and replace their correlator by a spacetime-local expression after Hubble-scale coarse-graining. This supplies the approximate reduced master equation.

sources.title: Decoherence of inflationary primordial fluctuations

evidence.text: Estimate post-reheating rates dimensionally using A = gv and an environmental operator B of mass dimension d. For illustrative quartic chaotic inflation, also estimate derivative-free cubic gravitational couplings; the paper finds them dominant over the potential-induced cubic coupling in slow roll.

sources.title: Inflation and squeezed quantum states

evidence.text: The two-mode evolution operator is factorized into squeeze and rotation operators. Composition over infinitesimal intervals gives first-order equations for squeeze factor Rk, squeeze phase Φk and rotation angle Θk; numerical evolution uses the associated recursion relations.

sources.title: Decoherence during inflation: The Generation of classical inhomogeneities

evidence.text: Represent the imaginary influence action with zero-mean Gaussian noises ξ₂ and ξ₃ and derive a semiclassical Langevin equation by variation. Renormalize its homogeneous specialization using adiabatic subtraction through second adiabatic order and dimensional regularization.

sources.title: Quantum to classical transition for fluctuations in the early universe

evidence.text: Environmental entanglement is estimated using the short-time de-separation coefficient A in w0(t)=1−At², where w0 is the probability of finding an unentangled state. Pointer observables are characterized by commutation with the interaction Hamiltonian and, for temporal robustness, approximate self-commutation at different times.

evidence.text: Could a preinflationary matter-like vacuum phase produce particles and entropy, supply an environment for gravitational decoherence, and thereby enable subsequent inflation to suppress vacuum energy without a complete quantum-gravity theory?

evidence.text: Deform nonforward amplitude contours into pole and cut integrals, and expand their Legendre partial waves to relate low-energy a_{p,q} to masses, couplings, and angular momenta. sources.title: Large Field Excursions from Dimensional (De)construction

evidence.text: Discrete Fourier transformation with 1/√N normalization diagonalizes the cyclic mass matrices. The gauge spectrum is Mg(n)²=4g²f²sin²(πn/N); comparison with n²/L² is made only in the formal continuum limit and for n≪N.

sources.title: Generic 3-point statistics with tensor modes in light of Swampland and Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture

sources.title: Large-field inflation and the cosmological collider

evidence.text: Compute the cubic-exchange bispectrum through an in-in integral of mixed propagators. WKB and saddle-point estimates explain its qualitative behavior; numerical evaluation uses Wick rotation and factors out early-time exponential mode dependence.

sources.title: Cosmological collider signal from non-Bunch-Davies initial states

evidence.text: Schwinger–Keldysh diagrammatics uses spectator Wightman functions built from Bogoliubov-transformed modes. Each propagator is decomposed into the BD term, a reversed-frequency term and two anomalous-frequency terms, with their respective Bogoliubov weights.

sources.title: Vector Dark Matter from Inflationary Fluctuations

evidence.text: Uses the separate-universes approximation for long inflaton perturbations, and Gaussian field contractions to obtain the density power spectrum as a convolution of field spectra.

sources.title: Primordial Black Holes and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Solve the reference tensor relation for its background amplitude, substitute into the target scalar relation, and infer the target response. Here the response is ε_PBH and the coefficient ratio is 1/16.

sources.title: Vector dark matter production at the end of inflation

evidence.text: For approximately constant ξ, use Whittaker solutions, massless Coulomb-function solutions and Bessel/WKB approximations, normalized to the initial Bunch–Davies vacuum. The stated WKB interval is 1/(8ξ)<−kτ<2ξ.

sources.title: Is the NANOGrav signal a hint of dS decay during inflation?

evidence.text: The reported workflow compares free-spectrum bin posteriors and power-law amplitude–slope contours with theoretical spectra. Named timing and sampling packages produced the contour plot, but the packet does not supply a reproducible statistical configuration.

sources.title: Oscillations in the stochastic gravitational wave background from sharp features and particle production during inflation

evidence.text: Use the radiation-era quadratic convolution of scalar spectra for ΩGW. Approximate individual scalar peaks by a delta-function comb to locate resonances, then smooth over finite peak widths to estimate modulation amplitudes.

sources.title: Resonant Vector Dark Matter Production during Inflation

evidence.text: Quantize transverse circular polarizations in Coulomb gauge and analyze Fλ″+[k²+a²m²±k df/dτ]Fλ=0 through Mathieu instabilities and Floquet growth. For constant frequency the quoted narrow-band estimates include q=γk/ω and μ≈γ/2.

sources.title: Gravity waves and primordial black holes in scalar warm little inflation

evidence.text: Can scalar Warm Little Inflation amplify small-scale curvature fluctuations near the end of quartic inflation enough to generate primordial black holes and an appreciable second-order gravitational-wave background while satisfying CMB constraints?
